static_traits.name: Li Jing
static_traits.social_status: Has several friends to confide in, but does not easily open up about self-doubt and insecurity
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; never treated for psychological issues before; denying history of similar issues
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, strong logic, able to notice and describe negative automatic thoughts; highly cooperative, positive attitude; emotions dominated by anxiety and uncertainty

basic_info.main_problem: I have always believed I am not smart enough and cannot write a novel; this belief blocks my wish to become a journalist.
basic_info.core_demands: When these negative thoughts began to affect my academic performance and overall health, I decided to seek counseling. I really want to find a way to get past these doubts.

core_beliefs: I am not smart enough/insufficiently capable
I am not as good as others

special_situations.event: In the writing workshop, classmates share work that is considered more polished and insightful
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my work is not as good as classmates', it means I am not smart enough and cannot become a writer/journalist either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: In workshops, mainly observes and speaks little, reducing exposure and evaluation; tries to suppress doubts with positive self-talk
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never beat them; I am just not smart enough.

special_situations.event: Difficulties and getting stuck when completing writing assignments
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my writing does not flow or I cannot finish well for a while, it proves I am inherently no good
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Procrastinates or avoids continuing to invest, lowering participation to avoid failure feelings
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This proves again I am no good; I cannot write anything meaningful.

special_situations.event: After starting a writing degree, exposed to more excellent writing and high-standard demands
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I still cannot reach a high standard now, I will not succeed in the future either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Frequently compares with others, lowering expectations in advance mentally to guard against disappointment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: At this rate, I am ultimately unsuited for writing and cannot become a journalist either.

special_situations.event: Every time I sit down to start writing
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Either I can write novel-level works, or it means I am not smart enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Over-self-evaluating before starting, hesitating, reducing attempts to avoid 'failure'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I cannot write a novel, it proves I am not smart enough.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as a capable writer, gaining a sense of competence and worth
core_conflict.fear: Fearing appearing inferior in comparison, being negated and humiliated, and ultimately failing
defense_goal: Avoids being evaluated and frustrated by reducing exposure and participation
Preventing disappointment through self-reproach and lowered expectations
Proving worth and fighting incompetence by pursuing 'perfect standards'

object_relations.self_representation: A student/writer with insufficient ability whose flaws are easily seen
object_relations.object_representation: Smarter and more critical judges (peers/readers/potential mentors)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When in sessions reviewing others' workshop works being praised, being invited to share, or talking about self-evaluation
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others or the counselor will see my inadequacies and negate me (viewing others as picky judges)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone self-blaming, lowering self-evaluation, using expressions like 'I am not smart enough/I am no good', avoiding elaborating concrete evidence of one's ability.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When directly focusing on current feelings (e.g. shame, anxiety) and exploring their sources
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Expressing emotions will expose weakness and bring negative evaluation
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Turning to talk about study plans or techniques, narrating in conceptualized, objectified language, reducing emotional vocabulary and details of subjective experience.

manifestations: Although having friends to talk with, finding it hard to open up about self-doubt and insecurity
Feeling alienated from peers amid comparison and self-denial
outcomes: Avoiding expressing vulnerable feelings, further worsening self-doubt and anxiety

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent self-denial ('I am not smart enough'), excessively worrying about being judged in interactions
More inclined to observe in workshops, speaking cautiously to avoid exposing 'inadequacy'

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains impulses to act toward other people or things, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to the self, turning originally outward energy against the self.
manifestations: When encountering writing difficulties and comparison situations, internalizing frustration and anger as self-blame and withdrawal
Reduces help-seeking and expressing needs, turns to self-reproach

positive_force: Has motivation to learn (pursuing a writing degree)
Has some social support (a few friends to confide in)
Has tried positive self-talk to counter negative thoughts
Actively seeking counseling and willing to test beliefs through action
negative_force: Core negative belief ('I am not smart enough') causing pervasive self-doubt
Excessive comparison and black-and-white thinking, cognitive distortions like predicting the future
Avoidance and withdrawal in key situations (reduced participation and expression)
Difficulty opening up vulnerable feelings to others, forming interpersonal tension and insufficient use of support
Academic setbacks and decreased motivation, forming a negative cycle

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated self-denial and negative thought rumination ('I am not smart enough/cannot write meaningful works')
antecedent: Attends writing workshops, sees peers' high-quality work
Sits down alone to start writing, encounters writer's block
Comparing abilities and achievements with others
target_behavior.core_reason: The inner core belief of 'I am not smart enough' being triggered, with self-verification through excessive comparison and catastrophic inference
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential failure and shame, gaining brief psychological protection (lowering expectations, temporarily reducing the anxiety of trying)
target_behavior.consequence: Declining academic performance, reduced motivation, interpersonal tension and reduced participation in interest activities

target_behavior.behavior: Avoidance and withdrawal in writing and communication situations (speaking less, avoiding sharing works and participating)
antecedent: Class / workshop settings where writing needs to be publicly displayed or discussed
Is invited to self-evaluate his work or receive feedback
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about being negated and losing face, internalizing external criticism threats as self-blame, reducing anxiety through avoidance
target_behavior.function: Escaping unwelcome stimuli (external evaluation, sense of failure), briefly lowering anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Lacks opportunities for practice and feedback, ability and confidence are further damaged, maintaining negative beliefs
